answer: The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, weighted by independent path length, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Every claim climbs the echo of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the velvet re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Reaching the harbor of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short.
